reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below $79,480.0 AND a failure to reclaim it on either of the next two hourly bars. Spot is 224.6 points above it, 0.46 hourly ATRs at the current 488.22 - inside the 0.4-to-0.6 ATR band that every gate collected in fourteen sessions was written in. The level is structural rather than round: it sits one point under the 1H EMA50 at 79,483.93 and immediately below the 79,500.0 liquidation rung where 295,096 USD of purely long-side fills landed in the last four hours. NOTE ON THE RECLAIM WINDOW: midday 27 August proposed extending the window from two bars to four whenever hourly ATR is CONTRACTING. That condition is not met here - ATR has ticked UP 1.4 percent from 481.68 to 488.22 - so the standard two-bar clause applies and the amendment is left untested for another session.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above $80,050.0. This gate is deliberately written OUTSIDE the trigger band and the desk is flagging that rather than hiding it: 345.4 points is 0.71 hourly ATRs, and the calibration log is explicit that a gate beyond half an ATR is a forecast, not a trigger. There is no honest alternative. The 80,000.0 handle carries the single heaviest realized-liquidation bucket on the board at 2,319,904 USD, and the log's own rule is not to write a gate at or under an uncleared shelf. 80,050.0 is the first level that clears both that shelf and the 15m EMA50 at 79,989.79. Expect it to fire late or not at all.

decisionBox.changed: Endday published REDUCE with gates at 80,150.0 / 80,600.0 and both resolved cleanly overnight. The REDUCE gate FIRED AND CONFIRMED at the 02:00Z close of 79,927.1, with 03:00Z at 79,812.9 and 04:00Z at 79,644.0 failing to reclaim - and it stays confirmed under the proposed four-bar window too, since 05:00Z closed 79,689.4 and 06:00Z closed 79,900.0. The ADD gate at 80,600.0 did NOT fire: despite a 81,499.9 print, no hourly bar settled above the line, the best being 80,580.0 at 00:00Z. That is the close-only discipline earning its keep for the second time this week - a wick-based gate would have bought the exact high. The box now moves from REDUCE to TAKE_PROFIT, and the reason is a genuinely new signal rather than a re-reading of old ones: the 1H carved a confirmed regular bearish RSI divergence, taking out the 25 August high of 81,280.0 by 219.9 points while RSI fell from 72.19 to 63.82. Concretely: a 15 percent slice of the spot core is booked here, the futures book is left flat after the overnight stop, and the remaining 85 percent of the core stays long because the 4H and daily frames are still above every EMA and the ETF bid was confirmed, not broken, overnight.

liquidation.note: 2,319,904 USD across 214 fills and only 26.2 percent short-side - so roughly 1.71m of it is LONGS being taken out. The honest caveat, unchanged from prior sessions: this is a record of where forced flow ALREADY happened on the way down through the level, not a wall of resting orders sitting there now.

1,731,406 USD across 297 fills, 95.8 percent short-side - the highest fill COUNT on the board, which means many small shorts rather than a few large ones. Together with the 81,000.0 and 81,250.0 rungs this is the fuel that produced the overnight spike, and it has now been spent.

1,039,661 USD across 203 fills, only 26.4 percent short-side. It is 45.4 points above spot, effectively at the market. 112,262 USD of it landed inside the last four hours and that recent slice is 91.9 percent LONG-side, so this rung is actively being worked right now, not historically.

527,179 USD across 88 fills, 23.8 percent short-side, and this is the important one for the next few hours: 295,096 USD of that total - 56 percent of the bucket - printed inside the last four hours and was 100.0 percent LONG-side. This is the freshest forced flow on the entire board and it is 204.6 points below spot. Longs have just been cleaned out here, which cuts both ways: the level has been defended, but the buyers who defended it are the ones who were liquidated.

167,431 USD across 29 fills, 0.0 percent short-side - entirely longs. Thin. Below it the 79,000.0 rung holds only 144,491 USD, also entirely long-side. That thinness is precisely why the invalidation is written at 79,250.0: there is very little mapped flow underneath to slow a break.

etfFlows.note: THE STREAK HELD AND ENDDAY'S WARNING RESOLVED THE BULLISH WAY. Endday reported the 27 August row as a provisional MINUS 41.0m with IBIT, BRRR and HODL still blank, and flagged explicitly that IBIT alone had supplied 200.8 of the previous day's 232.2 so a single late fill could flip it green. IBIT has now posted at +277.6 and the row settles at PLUS 242.3m: IBIT 277.6, BITB 21.7, ARKB 29.7, HODL 5.7, MSBT 6.7, BTC 11.7, against FBTC (83.6) and GBTC (27.2). The streak from 17 August is therefore NINE sessions - 297.5, 189.3, 517.2, 606.3, 307.5, 337.6, 314.3, 232.2, 242.3 - summing to 3,044.2m. The FBTC redemption of 83.6m is real and is the largest single-fund outflow of the streak, so the internals are less uniform than a week ago, but the headline is unambiguous: the institutional bid did not break overnight. This is the single most bullish input in this report and it is the main reason the box trims 15 percent rather than half.

Under the amendment adopted on 27 August - which requires two consecutive same-direction OI prints before open interest may override a trend signal - that threshold is now met, and it is met on a bar where the 1H frame has ALSO lost its EMA20 and turned its histogram negative, so the amendment's protective condition no longer shields the box. The retail long/short account ratio has climbed to 1.00 from 0.96 through the sequence 0.92, 0.97, 0.99, 0.98, 1.00, 1.00 - retail is no longer net short at all, so the short-covering fuel that powered Thursday afternoon is fully spent. divergences.note: A confirmed regular bearish divergence spanning 71 hours. The 2026-08-25T02:00Z hourly bar printed a high of 81,280.0 with Wilder RSI(14) at 72.19. The 2026-08-28T01:00Z bar printed a HIGHER high of 81,499.9 - clearing the old one by 219.9 points - with RSI at 63.82, a LOWER reading by 8.37 points. Higher price, weaker momentum. That same bar closed 1,002.7 points below its own high and the next four bars closed progressively lower, so the divergence is not a chart curiosity: it resolved immediately and with follow-through. This is the single piece of evidence that moves the tilt from bullish to bearish and it is the reason the box trims rather than adds.

calibration.rollingRecord: Fifteen sessions logged. Add gates fired and were collected on three consecutive sessions (27 August midnight, morning, and 26 August midday); midday 27 August produced the window's first whipsawed gate; endday 27 August's reduce gate has now fired and confirmed cleanly, and its stop was hit.
calibration.note: Endday's REDUCE gate at a settled 1H close below 80,150.0 FIRED AND CONFIRMED at the 02:00Z close of 79,927.1, with 03:00Z (79,812.9) and 04:00Z (79,644.0) both failing to reclaim - and it stays confirmed under midday's proposed four-bar window as well, since 05:00Z closed 79,689.4 and 06:00Z closed 79,900.0. The gate was placed 243.9 points out, 0.51 hourly ATRs, inside the band, exactly as the log prescribes. Its ADD gate at 80,600.0 did NOT fire despite a print of 81,499.9, because no hourly bar settled above the line; the close-only rule prevented a purchase at the absolute high of the move. acting_helped is TRUE. Endday trimmed the futures long from 45 to 22.5 USDT notional at roughly 80,393.9 and left a resting stop at 79,700.0; the 05:00Z bar traded 79,557.3 and took it. Half the size was already off, so the trim halved the loss on the stopped remainder. The honest caveat, and it matters: the 81,499.9 high came at 01:00Z, four hours BEFORE the 79,557.3 low, so a live desk would have collected the 81,280.0 first target on the full 45 USDT before the stop was ever threatened. The ledger's worst-case resolution rule - stop and liquidation take priority over take-profit regardless of chronology - books the loss instead. That is the conservative choice and the desk is not arguing with it, but the record should show that the trim helped against the LEDGER's accounting and cost roughly 0.19 USDT against the market's actual path. The finding to carry forward: endday's overnightRisk note named the ETF print as risk ONE and stated that a single late IBIT fill could flip the provisional minus 41.0m positive. It did, to plus 242.3m. Naming the resolution paths of a provisional number, rather than treating the provisional number as fact, is the practice that worked here and should be repeated.
